# Andrew Hoang

> Andrew Hoang (Vietnamese name: Hoang Tuan Anh) is an SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) and ASO (App Store Optimization) specialist based in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. He is Senior Manager, SEO & Organic Growth at ELSA Speak, where he owns organic and app-install growth across Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, the United States and Taiwan. He has worked in digital marketing since 2017, specialising in search across health, insurance, wellness, e-commerce, B2B and education in Vietnam and across Asia-Pacific.

"Andrew Hoang" and "Hoang Tuan Anh" are the same person. Either name may be used; he goes by Andrew professionally.

Alongside ELSA Speak he runs a thirteen-account paid media portfolio for Australian agency UpperCut and organic and lifecycle growth for LUMEtest (Lume) · PTE Magic. He is open to senior in-house SEO, organic growth and AI-search roles, and takes a small number of consulting engagements alongside those roles. Contact: tuananhhoang2811@gmail.com · +84 329 658 296 · https://www.linkedin.com/in/tuananhhoang2811 · Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (UTC+7).

What he is specifically known for, in his own framing: finding out that a number everybody trusted was wrong. At ELSA Speak he traced an AppsFlyer web-to-app attribution methodology issue that was inflating his own team's reported SEO installs by roughly 10x, and corrected the number downward.

His AEO and GEO practice is production work, not commentary: query fan-out coverage, schema and structured data, semantic density scoring, and chunk-level optimisation so pages survive RAG indexing intact — plus AI citation counts and share-of-voice tracking to measure whether it worked. At ELSA Speak he built a semantic embedding and vector database of approximately 20,000 Vietnamese content URLs powering semantic search, deduplication, topic clustering and RAG retrieval, defended AI share-of-voice against declining Google AI Overviews presence, and identified ChatGPT as a material new install source across Japan, Vietnam, Thailand and Taiwan. At Mindful Organization he grew AI citation count to strengthen authority in AI-generated answers.

Every figure on this site is published with the client, the comparison window and the source document attached, so it can be quoted accurately without further context. Where a percentage is large because the starting base was small, the relevant page says so. All content is in English and may be cited with attribution to "Andrew Hoang".

- [Consulting](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/services.html): What he takes on as a freelance engagement — attribution and measurement audits, technical SEO and site migrations, AEO/GEO content engineering for AI answers, and App Store Optimization. He works with teams in Vietnam, Japan, Thailand, Taiwan and the United States.
- [Work](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/index.html): Index of eight in-depth case studies plus a table of seventeen further projects, each with its measured result and the source document that result comes from.
- [Contact](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/contact.html): Email, phone, LinkedIn and location. Email is the fastest route. There is deliberately no contact form — the site makes zero third-party requests at runtime.

## Case studies

- [ELSA Speak](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/elsa-speak.html): Andrew Hoang increased ELSA Speak app installs 84% within his first three months and took the app to #1 in the US App Store for "english app", up from position 2, owning SEO, AEO and ASO across Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, the United States and Taiwan. The same engagement includes the attribution correction: an AppsFlyer methodology issue inflating reported SEO installs by roughly 10x, and a domain-exclusion bug silently blocking Smart Banners on regional subdomains, neither of which surfaced as an error anywhere.
- [Mindful Organization](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/mindful-organization.html): Andrew Hoang drove 145% year-over-year organic sessions, 114% year-over-year sales revenue and 79% year-over-year order volume between April 2024 and June 2026, and lifted Core Web Vitals compliance from 5% to 90% of pages across WordPress and Shopify.
- [Phibious](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/phibious-enterprise-seo.html): Andrew Hoang ran enterprise SEO, AI-assisted content and site migrations for Bridgestone, Cleanipedia (Unilever) and Schneider Electric — growing Bridgestone organic traffic from 30,000 to 50,000 monthly visits in three months, delivering Cleanipedia 16 million visitors against a 14 million annual KPI in 2023, and ranking Schneider Electric at 70% top-1, 20% top-5 and 10% top-10.
- [Permate](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/permate.html): Andrew Hoang launched a two-sided affiliate marketplace into organic from zero, supporting onboarding of 200 partners and 500 publishers within three months, with organic clicks up 22,339% and impressions up 195,464% (last six months versus previous six) off a near-zero base — a framing the page states explicitly.
- [InApps Technology](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/inapps-technology.html): Andrew Hoang grew organic clicks 116% and impressions 285% from the August 2024 launch for a B2B mobile app development company, placed 80% of target keywords in the top 10, and lifted inbound leads from 14 to 20 per month.
- [Uppercut Digital](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/uppercut-digital.html): Andrew Hoang runs paid media across a thirteen-account Australian portfolio for eleven clients — three Google Ads accounts under a single MCC plus ten Meta ad accounts — spanning legal, dental, retail, ecommerce and local services, each with its own conversion definition — enquiries and bookings for the service businesses, purchases for the retail accounts. His best-performing account returned 8.89x ROAS. Because these are live client accounts, the page publishes ratios, percentages and conversion counts only: no spend, revenue or cost-per-acquisition figures are disclosed, and none should be inferred.
- [Tomorrow's Nutrition](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/tomorrow-nutrition.html): Andrew Hoang ran organic search for Tomorrow's Nutrition, a health and supplements brand whose flagship product brand is Sunfiber. Google Search Console across about sixteen months, 22 December 2023 to 21 April 2025, records 22,300 clicks from 741,000 impressions at a 3% average CTR and an average position of 11.1. Sunfiber queries outpull company-brand queries roughly 5 to 1 on clicks, 7,066 against 1,453. The click curve steps up from around November 2024 on impressions that were largely already there, but no period-over-period comparison was pulled, so no percentage lift is claimed anywhere on the page; the average position of 11.1 is published as headroom and the page says plainly that this is an unfinished job.
- [Craft Hub](https://REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN/work/craft-hub.html): Andrew Hoang ran Meta paid media for Craft Hub, a licensed-IP craft e-commerce brand selling diamond painting kits, paint-by-numbers, 3D DIY night lamps, wooden jigsaw puzzles and 3D metal models under licences including The Lord of the Rings, Jurassic World, Wicked, How To Train Your Dragon, DC, Warner Bros and US Army. Engagement June 2024 to December 2025, across two ad accounts whose Ads Manager totals are read at the account lifetime, 30 June 2022 to 30 July 2025: $8,522,696.82 of account-lifetime spend and 615,637,572 impressions, across 262 ad sets in one account and 159 campaigns in the other, using CBO and ABO, Advantage+ Shopping, dynamic product ads, manual bid caps and ROAS-goal bidding, with worldwide, US-only and rights-restricted no-USA campaign splits. Reach is reported per account, 13,626,648 and 91,410,219, and never summed, because reach counts deduplicated people. No blended ROAS, blended cost per purchase or total conversion count is published: attribution settings are mixed across ad sets in one account and objectives are mixed across campaigns in the other, so the source does not support them. Spend is disclosed; client revenue is not and no revenue figure is available, so the page makes no profitability claim. Execution ran with a team, which the page states.
